subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before OAuth starts, or should OpenClaw design authenticated gateway-side credential forwarding?
rationale: Both options can fix the reported loss, but they make different product and security-boundary commitments for where OAuth credentials may be accepted and stored.

options.title: Block remote node-host login before OAuth
options.body: Treat non-loopback node-host gateway config as a wrong-host auth attempt and instruct the user to run login on the gateway host.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Add an authenticated gateway-side credential update flow with explicit protocol, authorization, and upgrade proof before allowing node-host login to continue.

options.title: Warn but still write locally
options.body: Keep local writes after a warning, accepting that users can still consume a token that does not update the active gateway.

recommendation.title: Block remote node-host login before OAuth
recommendation.body: Treat non-loopback node-host gateway config as a wrong-host auth attempt and instruct the user to run login on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the maintainer draft for this exact issue and has recent history in the affected auth command files.
